8	/-!
9	# The projective line over a field, with usable charts
10	
11	We define `AlgebraicGeometry.P1 k` as `Proj` of the standard graded polynomial ring
12	`k[X₀, X₁]` (`MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k` with the degree grading), together with:
13	
14	* `P1.structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k)`, and the instance `IsProper (P1.structureMap k)`
15	  (inherited from mathlib's properness of `Proj`);
16	* the two standard affine charts `D₊(X₀)`, `D₊(X₁)` (`P1.chartOpen`), which cover `P1 k`
17	  (`P1.chartOpen_sup`), together with the open immersions `P1.chartι i` from the affine
18	  models `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`;
19	* identifications of the chart section rings with polynomial rings:
20	  `P1.awayAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[t]` (the coordinate is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`).
21	
22	The identification of the chart *overlap* with Laurent polynomials, the section-level
23	versions, and the bundled chart package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` are in the
24	continuation file `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts`.
25	
26	The generic instance `Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x)` (for a graded `R`-algebra) and
27	the lemma `LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval` (*Laurent span*: every Laurent
28	polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a polynomial in `T⁻¹`) are general-purpose
29	and live in their natural namespaces.
30	
31	## Implementation notes
32	
33	We install `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a (project-global) instance: everywhere in this
34	project, `MvPolynomial` carries the standard degree grading. Mathlib leaves this to the user
35	because other gradings exist; this project only ever uses the standard one.
36	-/

65	  | add p q hp hq =>

378	theorem polyToAway_surjective {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
379	    Function.Surjective (polyToAway k i j) := by
380	  intro z
381	  have hz : z ∈ (⊤ : Submodule (𝒜 0) (Away 𝒜 (X i))) := trivial
382	  rw [← Away.span_mk_prod_pow_eq_top (X_mem k i) X (adjoin_gradeZero_range_X k)

384	  induction hz using Submodule.span_induction with
385	  | mem w hw =>
386	    obtain ⟨a, e, hae, rfl⟩ := hw
387	    refine ⟨Polynomial.X ^ e j, ?_⟩
388	    rw [map_pow, polyToAway_X]
389	    exact (away_mk_prod_eq k hij a e (by simpa using hae) _).symm
390	  | zero => exact ⟨0, map_zero _⟩
391	  | add u v _ _ hu hv =>
392	    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hu
393	    obtain ⟨q, rfl⟩ := hv
394	    exact ⟨p + q, map_add _ _ _⟩
395	  | smul c w _ hw =>
396	    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hw
397	    obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := (gradeZeroAlgEquiv k).surjective c
398	    refine ⟨r • p, ?_⟩
399	    rw [map_smul]
400	    change r • polyToAway k i j p = (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r) • polyToAway k i j p
401	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, smul_assoc, one_smul]

9	/-!
10	# Points of the projective line, and morphisms to it from chart data
11	
12	Two groups of results about `P1 k` feeding the construction of the finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
13	
14	**Morphisms into `ℙ¹` from an element of a ring.**  For a ring `A` under `k` (a morphism
15	`ρ : k ⟶ A` of rings) and an element `a : A`, `P1.fromSpecChart k ρ i a : Spec A ⟶ P1 k` is
16	the morphism through the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` sending the chart coordinate to `a`:
17	
18	* `P1.fromSpecChart_structureMap`: it is a morphism over `k`;
19	* `P1.SpecMap_fromSpecChart`: it is natural in `A`;
20	* `P1.fromSpecChart_isUnit`: **the gluing identity** — for a unit `u`, the morphism
21	  `[1 : u]` through chart `0` equals the morphism `[u⁻¹ : 1]` through chart `1`.  This is
22	  the entire content of "the loci `U_f` and `U_{1/f}` glue to a morphism to `ℙ¹`",
23	  concentrated in a single point-free identity: both morphisms factor through the chart
24	  overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`, where they are induced by the same ring homomorphism (the
25	  localization lift sending the overlap coordinate `T = X₁/X₀` to `u`).
26	* `P1.fromSpecChart_base_genericPoint`: if the evaluation `k[t] → A`, `t ↦ a` is injective
27	  ("`a` is transcendental"), the generic point of `Spec A` lands on the generic point of
28	  `ℙ¹`.
29	
30	**The topology of `ℙ¹`.**  `P1 k` is an irreducible, separated scheme; its charts have
31	Dedekind section rings, so its specialization order has height one
32	(`P1.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq`); and it has a point besides the generic one
33	(`P1.exists_ne_genericPoint`).  Consequently every non-generic point of `ℙ¹` is closed
34	(`P1.isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint`).
35	-/

87	/-- Every nonempty open subset of `ℙ¹` meets the chart `D₊(X₀)`: a point outside `D₊(X₀)`

90	theorem exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_of_isOpen {W : Set (P1 k)} (hW : IsOpen W)
91	    (hne : W.Nonempty) : ∃ z ∈ W, z ∈ chartOpen k 0 := by
92	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hne
93	  have hcover : w ∈ chartOpen k 0 ⊔ chartOpen k 1 := by
94	    rw [chartOpen_sup]; trivial
95	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at hcover
96	  rcases hcover with h0 | h1
97	  · exact ⟨w, hw, h0⟩
98	  rw [← opensRange_chartι k 1] at h1
99	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := h1
100	  -- The preimage of `W` in the chart is a nonempty open; so is the preimage of the
101	  -- overlap; the chart is irreducible, so they intersect.
102	  have hOne : ((chartι k 1).base ⁻¹' (chartOpen k 0 : Set (P1 k))).Nonempty := by
103	    obtain ⟨z⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of
104	        (Away 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1)))) := inferInstance
105	    have hpover : (Proj.awayι 𝒜 _ (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos).base z ∈
106	        Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1) := by
107	      rw [← Proj.opensRange_awayι 𝒜 _ (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos]
108	      exact ⟨z, rfl⟩
109	    have hp1 : (Proj.awayι 𝒜 _ (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos).base z ∈ chartOpen k 1 :=
110	      overlap_le_right k hpover
111	    rw [← opensRange_chartι k 1] at hp1
112	    obtain ⟨y', hy'⟩ := hp1
113	    exact ⟨y', by rw [Set.mem_preimage, hy']; exact overlap_le_left k hpover⟩
114	  have hdense : Dense ((chartι k 1).base ⁻¹' (chartOpen k 0 : Set (P1 k))) :=
115	    IsOpen.dense ((chartOpen k 0).2.preimage (chartι k 1).continuous) hOne
116	  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀W, hy₀O⟩ := hdense.inter_open_nonempty _
117	    (hW.preimage (chartι k 1).continuous) ⟨y, by rwa [Set.mem_preimage, hy]⟩
118	  exact ⟨(chartι k 1).base y₀, hy₀W, hy₀O⟩

183	/-- The evaluation of the section ring of the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` in a ring `A` under `k`,
184	sending the chart coordinate to `a`. -/
185	noncomputable def chartEval (i : Fin 2) (a : A) : CommRingCat.of (Away 𝒜 (X i)) ⟶ A :=
186	  CommRingCat.ofHom ((Polynomial.eval₂RingHom ρ.hom a).comp (awayToPoly k i).toRingHom)
187	
188	theorem chartEval_apply (i : Fin 2) (a : A) (z : Away 𝒜 (X i)) :
189	    (chartEval k ρ i a).hom z = Polynomial.eval₂ ρ.hom a (awayToPoly k i z) := rfl
190	
191	theorem chartEval_chartCoord {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (a : A) :
192	    (chartEval k ρ i a).hom (chartCoord k i j) = a := by
193	  rw [chartEval_apply, awayToPoly_chartCoord k hij, Polynomial.eval₂_X]
194	
195	theorem chartEval_algebraMap (i : Fin 2) (a : A) (r : k) :
196	    (chartEval k ρ i a).hom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) r) = ρ.hom r := by
197	  rw [chartEval_apply, AlgHom.commutes, Polynomial.algebraMap_eq, Polynomial.eval₂_C]
198	
199	/-- The morphism `Spec A ⟶ ℙ¹` through the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` sending the chart coordinate to
200	`a : A`; for `i = 0` this is the "point" `[1 : a]`, for `i = 1` it is `[a : 1]`. -/
201	noncomputable def fromSpecChart (i : Fin 2) (a : A) : Spec A ⟶ P1 k :=
202	  Spec.map (chartEval k ρ i a) ≫ chartι k i

204	/-- `fromSpecChart` is a morphism over `k`. -/
205	theorem fromSpecChart_structureMap (i : Fin 2) (a : A) :
206	    fromSpecChart k ρ i a ≫ structureMap k = Spec.map ρ := by
207	  rw [fromSpecChart, Category.assoc, chartι_structureMap, ← Spec.map_comp]
208	  congr 1
209	  ext r
210	  exact chartEval_algebraMap k ρ i a r

212	/-- `fromSpecChart` is natural in the ring `A`. -/
213	theorem SpecMap_fromSpecChart {A' : CommRingCat.{u}} (g : A ⟶ A') (i : Fin 2) (a : A) :
214	    Spec.map g ≫ fromSpecChart k ρ i a = fromSpecChart k (ρ ≫ g) i (g.hom a) := by
215	  rw [fromSpecChart, fromSpecChart, ← Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp]
216	  congr 2
217	  ext z
218	  change g.hom (Polynomial.eval₂ ρ.hom a (awayToPoly k i z)) =
219	    Polynomial.eval₂ (ρ ≫ g).hom (g.hom a) (awayToPoly k i z)
220	  rw [Polynomial.hom_eval₂, CommRingCat.hom_comp]

222	/-! ### The gluing identity -/

224	/-- The restriction of the chart `D₊(X₀)` to the overlap, as a factorization of the chart
225	inclusion of `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
226	theorem SpecMap_awayToOverlapLeft_chartι :
227	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (awayToOverlapLeft k)) ≫ chartι k 0 =
228	      Proj.awayι 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1) (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos := by
229	  rw [awayToOverlapLeft_eq]
230	  exact Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) one_pos (X_mem k 1) rfl
231	
232	/-- The restriction of the chart `D₊(X₁)` to the overlap, as a factorization of the chart
233	inclusion of `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
234	theorem SpecMap_awayToOverlapRight_chartι :
235	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (awayToOverlapRight k)) ≫ chartι k 1 =
236	      Proj.awayι 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1) (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos := by
237	  rw [awayToOverlapRight_eq]
238	  exact Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι 𝒜 (X_mem k 1) one_pos (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
239	
240	/-- The algebra structure of the overlap ring over the left chart ring is restriction. -/
241	theorem algebraMap_awayToOverlapLeft :
242	    algebraMap (Away 𝒜 (X (0 : Fin 2)))
243	        (Away 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1)) = awayToOverlapLeft k :=
244	  rfl
245	
246	/-- **The gluing identity**: for a unit `u` of `A`, the morphism `[1 : u]` through chart `0`
247	agrees with the morphism `[u⁻¹ : 1]` through chart `1`.  Both factor through the chart
248	overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`, where they are induced by the same ring homomorphism, namely the
249	localization lift sending the overlap coordinate `T = X₁/X₀` to `u`. -/
250	theorem fromSpecChart_units (u : Aˣ) :
251	    fromSpecChart k ρ 0 (u : A) = fromSpecChart k ρ 1 ((u⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A) := by
252	  have hunit : IsUnit ((chartEval k ρ 0 (u : A)).hom (chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
253	    rw [chartEval_chartCoord k ρ fin_zero_ne_one]
254	    exact u.isUnit
255	  set ψ : Away 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1) →+* A :=
256	    IsLocalization.Away.lift (chartCoord k 0 1) hunit with hψ
257	  -- `ψ` restricted to the left chart is the evaluation at `u`.
258	  have hleft : ψ.comp (awayToOverlapLeft k) = (chartEval k ρ 0 (u : A)).hom := by
259	    refine RingHom.ext fun z => ?_
260	    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, ← algebraMap_awayToOverlapLeft]
261	    exact IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq (chartCoord k 0 1) hunit z
262	  have hTu : ψ (awayToOverlapLeft k (chartCoord k 0 1)) = (u : A) :=
263	    (RingHom.congr_fun hleft (chartCoord k 0 1)).trans
264	      (chartEval_chartCoord k ρ fin_zero_ne_one (u : A))
265	  -- `ψ` sends the coordinate of the right chart to `u⁻¹`.
266	  have hSu : ψ (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) = ((u⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A) := by
267	    have hmul := congrArg ψ (awayToOverlap_mul_eq_one k)
268	    rw [map_mul, map_one, hTu] at hmul
269	    exact (Units.inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right hmul).symm
270	  -- `ψ` restricted to the right chart is the evaluation at `u⁻¹`.
271	  have hbase : (ψ.comp (awayToOverlapRight k)).comp (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 1))) = ρ.hom := by
272	    refine RingHom.ext fun c => ?_
273	    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.comp_apply, awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap,
274	      ← awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap, ← RingHom.comp_apply, hleft]
275	    exact chartEval_algebraMap k ρ 0 (u : A) c
276	  have hright : ψ.comp (awayToOverlapRight k) = (chartEval k ρ 1 ((u⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A)).hom := by
277	    refine RingHom.ext fun z => ?_
278	    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := polyToAway_surjective k fin_one_ne_zero z
279	    rw [chartEval_apply, awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply k fin_one_ne_zero]
280	    change (ψ.comp (awayToOverlapRight k)) (Polynomial.aeval (chartCoord k 1 0) p) = _
281	    rw [Polynomial.aeval_def, Polynomial.hom_eval₂, hbase, RingHom.comp_apply, hSu]
282	  -- Both morphisms factor through the overlap chart via `ψ`.
283	  have hfactor₀ : chartEval k ρ 0 (u : A) =
284	      CommRingCat.ofHom (awayToOverlapLeft k) ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom ψ := by
285	    ext z
286	    exact (RingHom.congr_fun hleft z).symm
287	  have hfactor₁ : chartEval k ρ 1 ((u⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A) =
288	      CommRingCat.ofHom (awayToOverlapRight k) ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom ψ := by
289	    ext z
290	    exact (RingHom.congr_fun hright z).symm
291	  rw [fromSpecChart, fromSpecChart, hfactor₀, hfactor₁, Spec.map_comp, Spec.map_comp,
292	    Category.assoc, Category.assoc, SpecMap_awayToOverlapLeft_chartι,
293	    SpecMap_awayToOverlapRight_chartι]

297	/-- If the evaluation `k[t] → A`, `t ↦ a` kills no nonzero polynomial, then the generic
298	point of `Spec A` (for `A` a domain) is sent by `fromSpecChart k ρ 0 a` to the generic point
299	of `ℙ¹`. -/

301	    (hinj : ∀ P : Polynomial k, P ≠ 0 → Polynomial.eval₂ ρ.hom a P ≠ 0) :
302	    (fromSpecChart k ρ 0 a).base (genericPoint (Spec A)) = genericPoint (P1 k) := by
303	  have hker : Function.Injective (chartEval k ρ 0 a).hom := by
304	    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
305	    intro z hz

307	    rw [chartEval_apply, awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply k fin_zero_ne_one] at hz
308	    by_contra hzne
309	    exact hinj p (fun h0 => hzne (by rw [h0, map_zero])) hz
310	  have h1 : (Spec.map (chartEval k ρ 0 a)).base (genericPoint (Spec A)) =
311	      genericPoint (Spec (CommRingCat.of (Away 𝒜 (X (0 : Fin 2))))) := by
312	    rw [genericPoint_eq_bot_of_affine, genericPoint_eq_bot_of_affine]
313	    refine PrimeSpectrum.ext ?_
314	    exact Ideal.comap_bot_of_injective _ hker
315	  rw [fromSpecChart, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, h1, chartι_base_genericPoint]

11	/-!
12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
13	
14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
16	
17	## Contents
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
25	  quasi-finite one.
26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
33	  docstring for the proof route.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` — the same finite `π`, now also carrying
35	  **dominance**, exported from the transcendence step of the construction
36	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1`). This is
37	  the map the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing class form consumes with no external dominance
38	  hypothesis.
39	-/
40	
41	set_option autoImplicit false
42	
43	universe u
44	
45	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial
46	
47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
48	
49	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
50	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
51	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/
52	theorem IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
53	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
54	    IsFinite π :=
55	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g
56	  IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite π
57	
58	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
63	
64	/-- A locally quasi-finite `k`-morphism from a scheme which is proper over `k` to the
65	projective line is finite. This is the Zariski-main-theorem half of the construction of the
66	finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`: it reduces finiteness to local quasi-finiteness. -/
67	theorem isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
68	    (π : X ⟶ P1 k) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = f) :
69	    IsFinite π :=
70	  have : IsProper (π ≫ P1.structureMap k) := hπ ▸ inferInstance
71	  IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp π (P1.structureMap k)
72	
73	end ZMT

75	/-- To produce a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹` it suffices to produce a locally quasi-finite
76	one; Zariski's main theorem upgrades it. -/
77	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
78	    (h : ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, LocallyQuasiFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
79	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
80	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hcomp⟩ := h
81	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hcomp⟩
82	
83	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
85	
86	/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
87	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
88	
89	This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
90	
91	Proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
92	1. `C` is integral (smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.
93	   GeometricallyReduced`, plus geometric irreducibility, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic`),
94	   and the function field of `C` contains an element transcendental over `k`: the étale
95	   coordinate of a standard smooth chart of relative dimension `1`
96	   (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField`, via the structure
97	   theorem for standard smooth algebras of Stacks 00T7);
98	2. the transcendental function spreads out to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`: the stalks
99	   of `C` are valuation rings (localizations of the Dedekind chart rings,
100	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections` and `Curve.StalksDVR`), so at each point
101	   either `f` or `1/f` is a regular germ; the two chart morphisms agree generically by the
102	   gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`, so the associated rational map `C ⤏ ℙ¹` is
103	   defined everywhere (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`);
104	3. `π` maps the generic point to the generic point (transcendence again), hence has finite
105	   fibers on the height-one Noetherian space `C`, hence is locally quasi-finite;
106	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/
107	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
108	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
109	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)
110	
111	/-- **Existence of a finite dominant map to the projective line.** On the smooth, proper,
112	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` which is
113	moreover **dominant**.
114	
115	The dominance is exported from the construction itself: the transcendental spreading-out
116	`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1` sends the
117	generic point of `C` to the generic point of `ℙ¹`, whose closure is all of `ℙ¹`. Zariski's
118	main theorem (`isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite`) upgrades the locally-quasi-finite map to
119	a finite one, preserving dominance and the compatibility with the structure morphisms.
120	
121	This is the FLV-4 frontier witness: it lets the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing headline and
122	class form (`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`,
123	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`) be
124	consumed with the *constructed* `π`, with no manually supplied `IsDominant` hypothesis. -/
125	theorem exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 :
126	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ IsDominant π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
127	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hdom, hcomp⟩ := exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1 C.hom
128	  haveI := hqf
129	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hdom, hcomp⟩

131	/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line
132	
133	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
134	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
135	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
136	affine), not how it was constructed. -/

140	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 k)
141	
142	/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
143	affine open. -/
144	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
145	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
146	  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π
147	
148	/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
149	theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
150	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
151	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
152	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
153	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
154	    trivial
155	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
156	  exact h

158	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
159	is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
160	`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
161	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
162	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
163	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)
164	
165	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of the chart
166	overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
167	polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/
168	theorem finite_app_overlap [IsFinite π] :
169	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
170	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
171	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)
172
